title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 187
paragraphs: That is the number of Xerxes's whole army. But of the women who baked bread for it, and of the concubines and eunuchs, no one can state an exact figure; nor, again, of the draft-animals and other beasts of burden, or of the Indian hounds that accompanied it — none of these could anyone count, because of their sheer multitude. So it does not surprise me that the streams of some rivers failed them; what astonishes me is how the provisions were enough to feed so many multitudes. For I calculate that if each man received only a quart of wheat per day and nothing more, the daily consumption would amount to 110,340 medimnoi — and I am not counting anything for the women, eunuchs, pack-animals, or dogs. Of all these men, so many myriads in number, not one was more worthy in beauty and stature than Xerxes himself to possess this power.
